status_summary: The administration moved in the opposite direction. On 2025-06-03 it doubled the Section 232 tariff on steel and aluminum to 50 percent, and when Executive Order 14389 ended the IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 it stated that Section 232 and Section 301 duties were unaffected. New Section 232 proclamations in August 2026 covered polysilicon (effective 2026-12-04) and unmanned aircraft systems (first duties from 2026-09-03), USTR added Section 301 tariffs of 10 to 12.5 percent on 60 economies on 2026-07-23, and on 2026-10-07 USTR gave notice that the 2018 Section 301 actions on China remain in effect pending a further review. A Section 232 proclamation of 2026-10-22 on wind turbines directed negotiations rather than new duties, and no removal of any Section 232, 201 or 301 action and no repeal bill was found through 2026-10-23.

timeline.event: Proclamation raises the Section 232 additional tariff on steel and aluminum articles and derivatives from 25 to 50 percent effective 2025-06-04 (UK remains at 25 percent).
U.S.-EU framework statement refers to Section 232 tariffs on pharmaceuticals, semiconductors and lumber and on autos, with a 15 percent ceiling for EU goods.
Executive Order 14389 ends IEEPA duties but states that Section 232 and Section 301 duties are not affected.
USTR imposes new Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies for failing to adopt forced-labor import bans, at 10 to 12.5 percent.
timeline.source: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

timeline.event: Proclamation 11052 (published 2026-08-11, 91 FR 51975) adjusts imports of polysilicon and its derivatives under Section 232, setting minimum import prices and an additional 15 percent duty on ingots and derivatives, with all-in rates of 15 percent for several partners and 10 percent for the UK, effective 2026-12-04.

Proclamation 11055 (published 2026-08-19, 91 FR 53699) imposes Section 232 duties of 100 percent and 25 percent on unmanned aircraft systems and some components, with the first duties effective 2026-09-03 and duties on other listed components from 2027-02-09.
Commerce (BIS) publishes a temporary final rule (91 FR 60505, effective 2026-09-22 through 2026-12-03) restricting stockpiling of polysilicon imports ahead of the Proclamation 11052 measures.

USTR publishes a notice (91 FR 64212) that, after receiving continuation requests from domestic producers and trade associations in the statutory four-year review, the two 2018 Section 301 actions on China remain in effect, and says it will conduct a review with a public comment process.

A proclamation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act on imports of wind turbines and their parts and components adopts the Commerce finding of a threat to national security, directs Commerce and USTR to pursue negotiations with trading partners with an update within 180 days, sets no new duty while allowing tariffs to be considered later, and leaves the existing Section 232 duties on steel, aluminum and copper unchanged.

title: Repeal Section 232, 201 and 301 tariffs and the underlying authorities
uncertainties: Proclamations for autos, copper, lumber, trucks, pharmaceuticals or semiconductors were not read; those are known here only from the EU framework statement and Federal Register titles in a 2026-09 listing. Current Section 301 rates on China were not read from a primary source (the 2026-10-07 notice gives no rates). Section 201 actions were not researched. Legislation in the 119th Congress on tariff delegation was not searched. A Federal Register API check for presidential documents mentioning Section 232 after 2026-08-01 listed only the polysilicon and unmanned aircraft proclamations and two Canada Section 338 scope modifications of 2026-09-14. A listing of presidential documents from 2026-09-08 through 2026-10-13 showed no tariff proclamation, but its second page was not opened. The 2026-10-22 wind turbine proclamation was read on whitehouse.gov and had no proclamation number or Federal Register citation as of 2026-10-23; the page's summary text describes an unrelated proclamation, while the body text is the wind turbine action. A White House fact sheet of November 2025 on a China arrangement said certain Section 301 exclusions were extended to 2026-11-10, and a USTR statement of 2026-09-08 concerned Section 338 duties on Canada; the first is a fact sheet and the second a statement under a different authority, so both are kept as sources rather than timeline events, and the underlying exclusion notice was not read.
